$comment: Where a catalogue variant could run on WaveSpeed instead of KIE.
Seed data for `pnpm providers:publish`, committed for the same reason
pricing.rows.json is: CI builds an empty database every run, so the rows
have to live in the repository.
EVERY ROUTE HERE IS SEEDED INACTIVE, and still is. On 2026-08-22 a real
WAVESPEED_API_KEY was used to check each path against GET /api/v3/models
— an endpoint their quickstart does not mention — and TWO OF THE FOUR
named a model that does not exist. Both were the ones whose `evidence`
said the path had been transcribed from a naming convention rather than
read off a page, so the warning was doing its job. Both are corrected
here, and each corrected path reproduces the saving in its `note` to
within a percentage point, which is the cross-check that they are right.
What is confirmed is that the paths resolve and that the adapter's error
handling is correct against the live API. What is NOT confirmed is any
success path: the account holds $0, so no generation has ever completed
here. data.id, data.outputs and the polling states remain read from
documentation. Activating a route still means finding out from a
customer's refund; run scripts/spike-wavespeed.ts once there is credit.
The four are the ones the provider analysis found WaveSpeed actually wins
on, out of the seventeen models both can serve. Everything else stays on
KIE, including all of Veo — KIE bills it flat per generation while
WaveSpeed bills per second, so the cheap Veo tiers are 4-8x more
expensive there.

provider.name: WaveSpeed
$comment: creditUnitName is 'usd' because WaveSpeed prices in dollars rather than
in a credit of its own. That makes its provider_credit_rates row read
1.0 — one unit is one dollar — and a price row's providerUnits for a
WaveSpeed model is simply the USD price.

rates.note: One KIE credit. Verified twice against the live table: Veo 3 Fast 80cr = $0.40, Nano Banana Pro 24cr = $0.12.
WaveSpeed bills in USD, so its unit is a dollar.

routes.name: Qwen Image (WaveSpeed)
routes.evidence: CONFIRMED 2026-08-22 against GET /api/v3/models, base_price $0.02. Parameters read off wavespeed.ai/docs/docs-api/wavespeed-ai/qwen-image-text-to-image; a POST with an empty body is rejected for a missing prompt, so the path validates.
routes.note: $0.02 on WaveSpeed against $0.02 of KIE credits; 4x cheaper and the coin price does not move, so the whole difference is margin.

paramOverrides.$comment: KIE takes aspect_ratio as a ratio string; WaveSpeed's qwen-image takes size as width*height. Renaming without translating would post '16:9' into a field that parses dimensions.

routes.name: Seedance 2.0 Fast (WaveSpeed)
routes.evidence: CONFIRMED 2026-08-22 against GET /api/v3/models, base_price $0.50. The transcribed path was right. Parameter names line up with ours: prompt, duration, aspect_ratio, resolution.
routes.note: -39% at 720p, the single best cost move in the catalogue. Parameter names already line up: prompt, duration, aspect_ratio, resolution.

routes.name: WAN 2.7 (WaveSpeed)
routes.evidence: CORRECTED 2026-08-22. The transcribed path wavespeed-ai/wan-2.7/text-to-video does NOT exist -- WaveSpeed answers 400 'Model not found.' The vendor prefix is alibaba, not wavespeed-ai. Confirmed against GET /api/v3/models, base_price $0.50, which reproduces the -17% below exactly.
routes.note: -17% at 1080p. Our variant names the aspect control `ratio` where KIE's other models use `aspect_ratio`, so the rename goes the other way here.

routes.name: Kling 3.0 (WaveSpeed)
routes.evidence: CORRECTED 2026-08-22. The transcribed path kwaivgi/kling-v3/text-to-video does NOT exist -- 400 'Model not found.' WaveSpeed splits v3.0 into std/pro/4k tiers; std is the one this note prices. Confirmed against GET /api/v3/models, base_price $0.42, which reproduces the -15% below.
routes.note: -15% for standard with sound. KIE is cheaper for standard without sound, so this route is worth activating only if the sound control is on.
